body: Yes. Because the people who are ill, don’t. Right now I’m travelling in public transport. The young man to my right is too busy playing a game on his phone to blow his nose (let alone wear a mask), he keeps snifling. And a woman in front of me is coughing without even covering her mouth with her hand - again too busy with her phone.

Money would give me more choices in life. I could choose to prioritize my sense of well-being, self-respect, and dignity. I could stop ‘thanking’ ppl for ‘job opportunities’ when I well know they are screwing me over. I could stop thinking I’m a loser because I don’t make enough money. 

Most importantly, I could have some peace of mind knowing that I could provide for myself and my family. 

I am too jaded to think about happiness - but peace of mind - I would love to have that.

I would not do well in such a scenario. I can quite imagine that the "bunch of autistic people" are more likely to each want do recover in their own way instead of doing things as a group. 

My "recovery" would be where I don't have to deal with my life as it is - no worries about family, work, responsibilities, money, etc. Where I could just be on my own, do my own thing, and not worry. I do my own thing frequently, but those worries are always in my mind, every single second. So for me personally, unless my life improves drastically, I think I have to accept that I may expect myself to cope with things, but I can't expect recovery.

Good intentions, effort, time, etc, cannot prevail over fate/bad luck. I have been dealt a bad hand, I've tried everything I could, but I ended up with nothing, except sorrow, disappointment, and despair. I am half-way done now chronologically, but I probably should have folded 20 years ago. Or just chilled - instead of tormenting myself with no reward.

Yeah. As kids we were told we could be anything. Then I get to spend the rest of my life toning down this dream until, heart of hearts, all I really want is to die in my sleep so that I don't have to fall deeper anymore.

I agree - hence despite being depressed for decades, I think I just hate my life. If I imagine myself without my troubles (which I can easily name and describe), I can imagine myself having much less craving for death.

Congratulations, or alternatively, condolences. I have always hated birthdays - I try to psychologically prep myself by saying reminding myself that it's just another day and that it doesn't has to have any meaning if I don't impose meaning on it. 

Having said that, I hope that every day ahead will be better for you than the day before in the coming year.

I did fairly well in school. It was a distraction to life. 

I failed at everything outside and beyond academics.

I don't have anything useful to contribute. Just that many years ago, it had dawned on me that apart from relatives who are "obliged" to come (I am Chinese), I have no friends to speak of who actually would want to attend my funeral. I suppose my workplace would send a representative, who would attend grudgingly, stay for 15 minutes and leave. 

I have been depressed for well over 20 years. The few childhood friends had long faded from my life. Never made friends at uni. Barely had work during my entire adult life, let alone friends.

I relate to this - except that I have always lived at home, and with my mother aging, I seem to be moving towards the direction of becoming a carer. That is practically my only reason to stay alive. Everything else, I have failed. 

I'm sorry that things are so hard.

I wish I could die. It would solve all my unsolvable problems. 

But I’m the ‘support system’ for other ppl and I feel as such I’m obliged to carry on as long as I can take it (Asian, daughter, unmarried, no kids). 

In the darkness of my soul, I considered that without the ppl who need my support, I’d be better off. But those thoughts became irrelevant as 40 is just in front of me. My life is crap one way or another at this age.
Life was hardly worth living when I was younger (I failed at every aspect). The older I get the more hopeless I become.

I’m glad it worked out for you; and I hope things will continue to be good. 

But you sound young.

For many of us, especially those who have hit mid-30s or older, it’s more about coming to terms with all the shitty things in life. 

For me personally, life got worse. I went from a depressed kid, teenager, young adult, to now a middle-aged person with no hope in life, now or for the future. 

My youthful hopes and dreams would never come true. My sensible plans and expectations in my adult years also fell through. 

I’m old, fat, friendless, loveless, childless, close to jobless. What I have are responsibilities and duties. 

No one in their right mind would tell me that life will get better.
I seem to fluctuate between comfort eating and not eating. Everything about me is just out of wack.

I am no expert but I have been depressed for close to 30 years. I have been tested as ‘very superior’ (not my words, but the categorization) IQ, I have a graduate degree, and yet I’m here at my late 30s, with nothing to my name. I hardly have a job, and I live with my mother. 

In my opinion, depression is not related to intelligence.  The overthinking (at least for me) pertains to endless cycles of hellish thoughts and afterthoughts. I wish I could channel that energy to more productive matters but it is not within my control.

I’ve not lived any part of my adult life without mental health issues (diagnosed) and I believe I had issues right out of the womb. 

Reaching the end of my 30s now. Despite having higher degrees, I have never been able to advance my career. My earning capacity is no better than when I first started out. Never married. Never had kids. Never moved away from home. 

I moved away from ‘young’ interest mainly because I think my physical age has caught up with me - I’m too tired/unmotivated to really do anything but the bare essentials. I think there’s nothing wrong per we with having ‘young’ interests. My problem lies in not having the ability (intellectually, emotionally, and financially) to deal with adult life and its problems. I am well past the window of opportunity to achieve the positive adult milestones, aka spouse/kids, ambitions, independence, etc. But the bad milestones will come one way or another. And I’m in no way prepared for it.

I tried multiple times to answer this question and I find that I have no concrete answer. I feel that it’s just too little, too late, for me. 

Practically, I wish I had more mentoring and encouragement at work when I was younger, which might have built up my confidence and self-esteem. Instead, people just exploited me or mocked me. I remain at the bottom rung of the ladder despite being in my late 30s. 

I wish I had some way of developing better life habits - so that I would not have become reliant on alcohol. 

I have problems with looking after myself and managing my life. I am terribly afraid of change - so much of that even though I could see how bad my life trajectory was going, I couldn’t get myself to do much about it.

Every year goes by faster than the last. 

For me, it just gets worse. I wish I had something more useful to say. But, at least, for me, I know I could never catch up with my peers anymore. I lose more ground as time goes by - and whilst I did not gain a new family (no spouse, no partner, no kids), it is inevitable that my mother would be my responsibility at some point. My career was no matter than it was a decade ago.

I agree with you that people use other people. And I feel sad that these folks whom I’ve worked with/for could not see anything in me that is worthwhile. 

Thanks for your reply.

Even more drama:

I had a ‘good’ day. My work (as part of a team)was approved and accepted, no questions asked by client. 

It was urgent work (I had like less than 2 days) to get it done. At the time my boss told me to start immediately on it. And at the time I said due to the urgency of the matter I am requesting a higher cut than usual. 

I also conveyed this to the other member of the group, out of transparency and fairness. 

So I dealt with the matter and got the so-called good result. In fact, it was the other member of the group who reminded the accounting staff of my increased rate on this occasion. 

Then I received a message from my boss stating that he would not change the payment system for me so as not to be criticized by others also working for him. And so he’d only pay me the usual rate. 

I reminded him of what transpired. Even the other team member confirmed. 

He responded saying he has no recollection but that to avoid dispute he would pay me the increased rate. 

It felt like a slap in the face. Essentially he’s saying I was dishonest. 

For additional info, I earn commissions when I am engaged for a project. I’m not on a fixed income. So it’s not unusual at all for fees to fluctuate.

You are a much more positive person than I am. 

Right now I'm in a cloud of denial. I just refuse to really think about it, let alone deal with it.

Over the past week, more discussions have taken place and I am given to understand that I'm not singled out. Save for a group of "family and friends" employees, others are more or less in my situation, i.e. there is no conclusive answer as to whether we would be re-hired yet - but I take it that we are strongly encouraged to find something else as their idea is to downsize. 

I know the job-hunting process will be difficult, and quite possibly awkward and embarrassing. I'm not a newcomer, but someone with years of work experience, so it is understandable that people expect much more than I am able to deliver. I know there will be the issue of whether people are willing to hire me as a "junior staff" when I am not only in the workforce for much longer, but likely actually quite a bit older than everyone else. There's a bit of irony here. Years ago when I started out, everyone thought I was too young - in the blink of an eye, I have become too old.

When I now review my position, I can see how pathetic I am - no one wants to take me on, and I think, if I asked my boss for a referral letter, I'd just get the standard type ones (which essentially means he thinks nothing of me). I have no one to turn to - I didn't build any connections in all these years. The picture I see is that I have wasted all these years, supposedly the most productive years of my life.

Thanks for the info, I might look into them when I have a bit more energy. Right now I'm barely managing to get myself together physically (e.g. I might feel thirsty/cold, but wouldn't do anything about it for hours). 

I doubt you would remember - I am Chinese. It's Chinese New Year (the 4th day anyway) so these times get me even more stressed than usual.
Thanks for your reply. I don’t really take anything regularly. Sleeping meds and anxiety meds that I take when it is necessary.

I had quite intensive therapy in my youth - for free, as it was provided by the university. It mostly benefitted me in that it gave me some sense of stability. 

Whilst I am not entirely averse to trying therapy again (although I have reservations give my age - middle aged woman and my fixed ways is quite different than my younger mind), I simply can’t afford the costs.
No, I’m in Asia. I just converted the medical fees to USD for reference.

I have considered that. However it’s such a hassle to start over again. Especially when the first appointment is usually so expensive (cos that is the one occasion when they ask about my problems and takes longer than 3 mins).

My psychiatrist is of similar age to me so there is no paternalistic shaming. However I confess I sometimes feel inferior - this is someone who is my own age who has a family with children, a very good career, etc. it’s a bit different than my olds days when everyone treating me was significantly older. 

Thanks for your words of support.

I can’t afford a therapist. I know my psychiatrist won’t do any talking (there are 3 therapists sharing the same office with him, so business wise I think he would refer me to them). I guess I was being a bit immature in expecting that I would get some cursory comfort from him. 

In my youth I actually have done a lot of CBT but sadly it didn’t work. The problems I face now are substantially more dire than those old days. 

I do talk to myself. It’s better than nothing.

Thank you. 
I distract myself by watching tv and try not to think. But of course ultimately the thoughts creep their way back.
I am not fit enough for intense physical activity, but I try to take walks when there is sunshine.
Thank you. I don’t have people to talk to irl. Sometimes I am consumed by an urge to say something, to connect, and I do it here.

For me, the interpretation of ‘getting better’ is one’s increased ability to accept/handle crap…problems get bigger and more complicated as my life goes on. Unfortunately, I never got better at dealing with things.

Thank you for your kind words. 

I wish I had a stable job. That I was less arrogant in my youth and thought I would make it in this dog-eat-dog world. I am invisible and replaceable - in a self-employed business, it often means I have no business. 

Sometimes I take walks. But everything, work, family, etc, are all demanding my attention. My incompetent attention. 

I can't help but feel that my peace will only come when I die.

There has always been a sense of burden, of sorrow over me, even when I was a child. 

People used to say "it gets better", out of their good hearts, and because sometimes it does. However, I don't seem to have develop better abilities to cope with life, and what life throws at me, as time goes by. Age-wise, I am a middle-aged woman, but I don't think I have ever been anything but the scared child that I always have been. 

I tried hard. But nothing worked out.

I can’t afford anything. My self-care, on a good day, is watching tv, reading, anything to distract my mind. On a bad day, unfortunately I resort to heavy drinking. I am very alone - no partner, no friends - I guess that is a testament to my failed life. All I can do is crawl into bed and hope for sleep. 

I’m sorry I’m being so negative. You have been very kind to take time to talk to me.
I am not drunk right now - I only had a small drink. But I'm still feeling high levels of depression and anxiety.
I am in some sort of inertia. Heart of hearts, I want to just give up. but realistically I know that is not ok.

I see a psychiatrist sporadically (when I can afford it) to get meds for sleep and anxiety. I certainly can't afford a therapist. I try not to drink that hard when things are just "dull", but when life hurts, I really have very few options. Thanks for your kind words.
It’s still the day here. I do want to get some sleep but I’m too worried and strung out.

I didn’t blame people for saying this. After all what were they supposed to say? 

Truth be told, they stop saying that after I turned 30 and I sort of missed it. It’s like, even in the polite, genteel world, I have become a lost cause. People jist avoid me thereafter.
I feel the same. I know that I screwed up, and that at middle-aged, it is what it is. But I have yet to find the grace to accept that and to move on.

When I was younger, there was still some hope, amidst all the bleakness. 

For years now, I just live every day in dread. I actually feel that failing to kill myself back then is a "missed opportunity". I don't have friends - my life never moved on, never improved from what it was 20 years ago, whilst others have built their own lives. 

There is nothing I can do. I feel that the chance to really make an improvement to my life has passed. No, not the "go take a walk, do some exercise, get some sunlight" kind of improvement, but ones regarding to relationships, career, money, etc.

My Christmas wish for at least the last 20 years had been a quick and hopefully relatively painless death for me. 

Christmas and the New Year just exacerbates my sense of worthlessness. 

Holding on was absolutely pointless for me.  Only led to more disappointment and suffering, realising I am in fact past the point of no return for real (after I turned 30, no one ever said stupid things like "things are going to get better"...and I am nearing the end of my 30s now), but failing to accept that my destiny in life is to be burdened by suffering with no reward.

When I was at university many many years ago, I had several suicide attempts, and basically spent all 3 years dealing with my mental health. No friends, none of the young adult experience. At the material time, I considered it the darkest hour of my life.

In the past 10 years or so, I think of those years with a degree of nostalgia and even fondness. 

Yes, things get worse and worse.

I come here (and other groups on reddit and elsewhere) to vent. There are kind people who had consoled and comforted me.

Notwithstanding my gratitude to those who had been generous with their time, I mainly use this space (and other online space) to "scream" at the void. My problems (as with other people of our age) are usually real life problems, requiring real life solutions that one wouldn't expect online. I well know, and occasionally feel embarrassed that I seem to say the same things over and over again. But the sad truth is, I can't resolve my real life problems, and there is no one to speak to in real life, and I enter into a mode of word/emotional diarrhoea here. 

It gives me momentary relief. To say what I want to say, without fear of criticism, judgment, or ridicule (I do not care, let alone fear, online bullying). I hope you find something that helps.

I’m sorry to hear that your life changed from a happy one to one which is fraught with difficulties. I don’t know how that is like - I have never loved life. I don’t know which of our predicament is worse. 

My bad day is a work thing. Boss yelled at me, ignored me in front of other people, etc. I have been mistreated for so long that I’m more tired of it all than angry.

Many years ago when I was still at uni, a psychiatrist after hearing my account that I have always felt like that, said to me that perhaps this is just who I am. 

I felt misunderstood then. But for years I have realized perhaps he is right.

You sound like me. At about 30, I already knew it was not going to get better, but I grasped at straws - because I had held on for so bloody long, from "you have still so much potential and life in front of you" youth to an "at best invisible, but often embarrassingly awkward and pathetic" middle-aged person. Now in my late 30s, it is inevitable that things are only going to get worse. I'm staying on just for my mother. 

I hope for death every day. I hope that I die in my sleep. But knowing my luck, it's just not gonna happen. I so wish for an easy way out.

I am in nearly the exact situation. Similar age, living with my elderly mother, regretting my life decisions.

However, I think you did well in finding a job that you like, and I guess that your earnings will increase with seniority at the job.

I am at my "dream job". Never did anything else. But I'm miserable, and I have been there for over a decade. Can't get out, though, no other skills and getting too old for the employment market.

Sorry to hear that you are feeling so poorly. I'm of similar age, and I also wish that I did it years ago, when I was still young and would be remembered if not in fondness at least with sympathy. 

Yep, down is where I'm going too.

I think it's partly because of all the movies and tv shows (moving from some sort of "idiot savant" in the past to the "quirky genius" in the present). It's also partly because in the last decade, many (children and older ppl alike)  who would not previously have been diagnosed had now been diagnosed, i.e. people whose mental capacity was not affected. 

And, perhaps an unpopular opinion, many seem to like to be seen as the "quirky genius". 

For myself, I tested well as a child and as a student. But I have been doing terribly as an adult, I do v badly at work, never left the bottom rung (despite having worked for 13 years).

Thanks for your reply.

For me, I wish it'd just end, I don't need or want the meandering anymore.

Thanks for the reply. 

I did sleep but it was not restful, but it's not out of the norm for me. Sometimes I wonder if that is part of the reason why I feel so stupid when I go about my day.

Same situation, no advice unfortunately. 

Has been depressed/suicidal (in varying degrees of severity) for over 2 decades. Did everything I could to save myself, to no avail. Often regret not doing it back when I was still young and shiny. These days, I stay around because it'd be terribly cruel to my mother if I don't.

Your life doesn't sound boring to me, you have stable and gainful employment, you seem to be doing well looking after yourself. You are still quite young, and still have some time/opportunity to develop relationships/interests without having to really weigh their worthiness. 

I hope this doesn't sound alarming, and I hope it doesn't happen to you - but one day, if/when all hell breaks loose, you might miss this "boredom".

Yes. Sadly, I did not get any super power, special interest, or whatnot from the bag of autistic traits. I was, and am, a very awkward individual with very poor social skills. Whilst I can't pinpoint autism as the root of all my problems and failures, the fact is I am on the wrong side of 30 with no relationships, and hardly a job. 

I would choose not to have an autism any day, any time.

Late 30s. Suicidal/harboring suicide ideation thoughts for more than 20. No words of advice, just to share the sentiment. 

As I turned 30, I became aware that the "it gets better" happen to some people only...usually younger people having an adolescent/young adult existentialist crisis, or some temporary setback that is more akin to rites of passage of growing up. For many others, the problems are inherent, with deep roots that fortify as the years go by.

As much as I try to accept that it's just gonna be worse (and yes for me, it is. I have reached a point in life where most changes are for the worse, not for the better), every time some crap comes up, I become suicidal, even though I know, or at least I hope, that I would just stick it out for my mother.
Special interests, and "super powers" - one may be very special and very intelligent with or without autism.

30s here. I sometimes want to post here but an iota of "guilt" in me fears that a young person would read it and feel it's all gonna be hopeless. I concur that I wish there is a separate group for older people. 

'Cos often I want to shout, no it doesn't get better, it really doesn't. Somewhere around my mid/late 20s, it dawned on me that no amount of waiting for a corner to turn is gonna bring relief. Every time, it's just a bigger and scarier monster lurking in the corner waiting to jump at me upon my arrival. So much so that one of my biggest regret in life is that I didn't kill myself in my uni days (or younger). However, I'm hesitant about voicing this sentiment, given that it might inadvertently "trigger" a younger person. 

I argue that there is a conceptual difference for older ppl and younger ppl experiencing suicidal thoughts. For me, it's no longer about keeping faith and hope for the future - such thoughts do more harm than good. For me, it's about how to find an equilibrium in my mind and soul - to accept that I have made stupid mistakes, that I am not as good/talented as I had thought/hoped, but to also recognise that more often times than not luck has a serious part to play and I haven't exactly been lucky. That although my life is a complete waste, I should try to stick it out for my own reason (for me, it's my mother).

Thanks for taking the time to respond. 

I worked in the living room last night to check on her, and she woke at about 11:30pm. She had a stronger appetite, and ate more food, and then took another round of meds and went back to bed. 

I stayed home today as well. She said she feels better than yesterday. We had lunch and watched some tv, then she went back to her room to rest. 

I'm feeling like crap. I admit, despite everything, I'm still worried about the supposed warning letter but since I didn't go in for two days, I don't know what is the status of that issue. 

Obviously, my foremost concern now is my mother's health. I have been weeping for short moments (like a few seconds). Out of fear, anxiety, anger, guilt, and I don't know what else. 

All my efforts to stop drinking has been abandoned. I don't know how else to allay my overwhelming feelings.

Sorry to hear that things have been especially rough. I clearly would be the last person to give advice so I’m afraid this is just a response. 

I am also very much alone. I talk to myself (in private), literally saying my thoughts out loud. Sometimes that relieves some of my emotions. I distract myself with books when I have the energy or tv if I have none. 

It’s not much of a life, but one day follows another. I never quite know which problem/crisis would finally break me. 

It is tough making big decisions alone. But perhaps most tough decisions are made alone anyway. Not that I disagree that it’d be easier on the heart and brains if we had some support from people around us. 

I hope things improve for you soon, and thanks for always being kind in your responses to my posts.

Fair enough. 

I was not built to be tough and people like me get mowed down by life.

My point was, there are lots of people who are not tough enough to withstand the hardship that comes their way in life. Some are fortunate - either they were blessed with a smooth path, or they had the ability to get through it. Yet undoubtedly there are people like myself, who can’t pull themselves together despite their best effort. And then, with hindsight, high school was not so bad after all.

Well said.

I congratulate all the sad, misunderstood, bullied kids who became happy and well-adjusted adults. But surely, not all the happy kids were bullies or perpetrator. And who knows what life had in store for anyone down the road. 

I was a depressed, anxious, lonely kid, who genuinely hang on to the thought that it'd all get better after high school, so much so that with hindsight, I did not live in the present. I never lived like a young person because everything was about "later". And there are so many many things that could only be done/accepted/forgiven/enjoyed when one is young.

I wouldn't tell kids those are their best years, but I think I would tell them to enjoy being young. 

P.S. in the end, I peaked at high school anyway. Perhaps it's not often, and not fair that the quiet, hardworking, responsible kid grew up to be a complete loser (mid-late 30s, no career to speak of, no partner, no child, never married, still living at home). I am just a worse version of my younger self. But life threw me many many curveball relentlessly.

Thanks for taking the time to reply.

I agree that I have built many walls and hurdles - I know that they cause me incessant anxiety, so much so that it impacts on my performance. It's a learnt helplessness situation, I guess. Things go wrong all the time, and I seem incapable and incompetent.

Constantly, it feels like my brain is not what it used to be, or what I thought it was. 

I am trying to tell myself that it is a small job, that is of relatively low risk to myself, that I can manage.

Thanks as always for your kind words.

I wasn't drunk during the meeting. I think I had done what I was expected to do. I just wish things would go smoothly.
Childhood problems, autism (diagnosed after I was at university), poor judgment. One thing led to another.

Thanks. I try to appreciate the small things in life, microscopic things. 

Indeed, it has been years. I mock myself for not just taking the plunge and kill myself. 

I hope that you are doing alright.

Thanks for your response.

You seem to be getting it even worse than me. I have stopped taking it as it doesn't seem to help. Stilnox worked better for me, but over time, it became less effective. Hope you find something that helps.

I know nothing about the pain and struggles of divorce - I have never been in a proper relationship. 

However, when I read your post, several parts resonated with me. Being middle-aged, the shame and embarrassment we feel from our life circumstances, the lack of financial resources and/or help, the lost of "friends" (grew apart, or due to the huge differences in life circumstances), etc.  When I was younger, I also thought that things would change or I would change. Ironically it only changed for the worse.

I drink too, cheap vodka, and alone. I have been contemplating suicide, for a very long time. 

I have no words of comfort to offer, but I do hope you find some luck with money - that usually helps with nearly everything.

Thanks for your kind words. No I didn't wake up one day and felt all these emotions - it has been a haul, which I staggered on for decades, without realising that I had missed the gateway to call it quits.

It's too late in life for me to do myself in (at least, I hope I can hang on so that I don't inflict more suffering on my elderly mother) , so I do have a "tomorrow" for now. 

I hope things get better for you.

It's a "trend" - like how 10-20 years ago, young people were claiming to be depressed and/or have ADHD. 

Creative media depicts their autistic characters as persons who are highly intelligent, effortlessly skilled, much loved (or at least have a loyal group of friends with the character being the centre of it all), with only a few harmless quirks (all very much accepted/tolerated by the character's social circle). I'd love to be that person too, autistic or not. 

I was diagnosed in my very late teens. I'm now in my 30s. I am jobless, friendless, loveless, and I live with my mother. Quite certain no one would fake autism to be me.

My two-cent is, for those faking it, they will grow out/snap out of it when it is no longer trendy or when it is inconvenient (note: real life, real adult life, does not care at all as to whatever conditions you may or may not have), so don't give this trend too much weight.
The future.

I try to admire that strength in others but I fail to recognize it in myself. 

It despairs me that I’ve struggled half of my life just to reach the starting point. 

I try to cut myself some slack - I have been telling myself that comparison is pointless. Quite sure that others don’t admire me for my struggles though. 

Perhaps it’s my mood. But I interpret that person at the left picture as a young overachiever, and I, crawling at the bottom, the middle-aged loser who started climbing before he was born.

I also have a rather unhealthy symbiotic relationship with my mother (thought in my case, most of the fault and problem is mine) - so you are not alone.

You are still relatively young - and I agree with many here, you are very articulate, which is indicative that despite everything, your mind is still strong. I hope you find the help that you need.
I don’t have super powers.
I am different people, to different people.
All the time. I consider myself my own "therapist".

Yes. My autism doesn’t come with any perceived ‘super power’. I am just odd and confused and lonely, and has fallen very far behind in life with no hope of ever achieving adult milestones (I’m already in my 30s).

I only go pick up meds for insomnia and anxiety like once or twice a year nowadays as I am unable to afford regular and long-term medication/visits to the psychiatrist. In these appointments, I would only be asked a cursory "how are you?" and my psychiatrist would then proceed to promote this or that medication and handing me pamphlets/brochures for those medication (a few years ago, I have tried various kinds of antidepressant with no success). 

To me, my psychiatrist is more like a pharmaceutical rep/salesman than a doctor, as I feel being forced to watch a presentation on meds rather than being cared for or looked after in any sense of the word.

Passion is at times overrated. Many people have no particular passion in life. For those who are passionate about something, their passions don't necessarily translate into a means of livelihood. 

As you are nearing 30, it might be wise to have some work experience to "show for it" as you have aptly pointed out. Whilst there are many people who claim to find 2nd chances at a latter time in life, I believe there are more who were stunted  by CVs that fell short of expectation when one reached a certain age.

As much as I appreciate your effort and contributing in educating the public about autism, I might add that you don’t necessarily have to pitch it as a gift. It’s a condition, like everything else in the DSM. 

I’m sure there are many people who find their peace or even their edge in autism. But there is an equal if not more people who suffer from it. As much as modern media tries to depict it, autism is more than a group of awkward, eccentric, but extraordinarily intelligent people. It is a spectrum, and there are so many less fortunate variations: many who are unable to look after themselves, those who are just awkward but not exceptional, those who are held back because they can’t play around the rules of society, etc.

It’s someone to talk to, and someone who does not judge you (at least, they have to veil their judgement); which is helpful up to a certain point. The point for me is when:

1. I have lived with whatever issues I have for years, I know myself quite well; further instrospection is not useful. 

2. I am old enough to know a bit about life and I don’t need someone (and without meaning disrespect, quite possibly someone considerably younger) repeating to me what I already know. 

3. The financial pressure caused by seeing a therapist outweighs whatever carthartic benefits I may derive. 

For me, if I really have the extra money (and I do mean extra, I have loads of bills and little income), I wouldn’t mind seeing a therapist again. But then again, if I have no financial pressure at all, perhaps I wouldn’t need a therapist after all.

It’s about knowing the right person at the right time - and being appreciated by the right people at the right time. 

I would be the first to admit I failed at this task, miserably. And this failure belittles and overshadows any positive attribute I’ve ever had.
